As a real estate agent, I’m constantly meeting new people—clients, colleagues—and I feel like they’re always staring at my face. I’m convinced the left side of my nose is different from the right, and no mirror, no camera, not even my doctor’s reassurance helps. I spend hours each day checking it in windows, phone screens, any reflective surface I can find.  

I catch myself looking at people around me—on Zoom calls, at open houses—comparing their noses, their jawlines, their skin. I even pause celebrity interviews, frame by frame, trying to prove I’m not imagining it. My ex-husband said I’ve changed, that I’m not sleeping, not going out unless I "look okay," which is never.  

I know it sounds extreme, but I’m not crazy. I don’t hear voices or think the government is watching me. I just *know* something’s wrong with my face—so wrong that I sometimes cancel showings last minute. I’m not paranoid. I’m not losing touch with reality—just with myself.
